prompt:
Research the official free-tier limits of the GitHub Actions service for public and private repositories (minutes, storage, concurrency). Cite the GitHub documentation page you used.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the official free-tier limits for GitHub Actions based on the documentation:

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-where-workflows-run/choose-the-runner-for-a-job | QUOTE: "Use of the standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited on public repositories." | CLAIM: For public repositories, GitHub Actions provides unlimited free minutes when using standard GitHub-hosted runners.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Actions usage is **free** for **self-hosted runners** and for **public repositories** that use standard GitHub-hosted runners." | CLAIM: For public repositories, GitHub Actions usage (which encompasses both minutes and storage) is free when using standard runners.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/man
